risks: _legend() | low | Returns HTML with hardcoded f-string using 'reach' and 'sw' variables not defined in this chunk; if those are missing at call site, KeyError or NameError will occur. | Verify that 'reach' and 'sw' are in scope when _legend() is called.

handoff.purpose: Defines _legend() returning HTML for reachability notes, and render_html() constructing the full HTML page header with stamp, gate, toc, narrative, and legend.

symbols.name: _legend
symbols.note: Returns an HTML <ul> with hardcoded explanatory text about reachability categories; uses variables 'reach' and 'sw' that must be in scope.

symbols.name: render_html
symbols.note: Assembles the full HTML page header from 'data' and 'narrative' dicts; includes stamp, gate, toc, narrative sections, legend, and class legend.

claims.text: The single largest judgement call is the main_guard entry kind: a module with a __main__ guard is runnable as python -m and counts as a way in. Drop that rule and materially more modules go dark. The kind is recorded on every module so the call can be re-litigated without re-running anything.
claims.why: The claim refers to 'main_guard' entry kind and its effect on module reachability, but the chunk does not contain any code that implements or records such a kind. The claim is about behaviour outside this chunk.

claims.text: The stamp says WHEN this ran and WHAT WAS ON DISK. It is allowed to claim 'and that is revision X' only when both halves of that claim were checked.
claims.why: The comment describes the semantics of 'stamp' keys, but the chunk does not show the stamp generation or validation logic. The claim is about behaviour outside this chunk.

claims.text: The working tree was DIRTY when this page was generated (X paths).
claims.why: The code checks stamp['dirty'] == 'dirty' and generates a note string containing the dirty paths, matching the claim.

claims.text: Whether the working tree was clean could not be determined.
claims.why: The code checks stamp['dirty'] == 'unknown' and generates a note stating that cleanliness could not be determined, matching the claim.

claims.text: X of the python files counted on this page are NOT TRACKED by git, so they are in no revision and the dirty probe above cannot see them (sample).
claims.why: The code checks stamp.get('untracked_scanned', -1) > 0 and constructs a note with the count and optional sample, matching the claim.

claims.text: Whether the scanned files are tracked by git could not be determined.
claims.why: The code checks stamp.get('untracked_scanned', -1) < 0 and generates a note stating that track status could not be determined, matching the claim.

claims.text: This page describes WHAT WAS ON DISK when it ran; it is not a description of revision X.
claims.why: The code appends a note saying exactly that when there are any notes (dirty, untracked) or when describes_revision is not set. The comment matches the generated HTML string.

claims.text: Working tree clean and every scanned file tracked: what this page describes is revision X.
claims.why: The code checks stamp.get('describes_revision') and appends a note stating the page describes that revision, matching the claim.
